 Home Business News ITR Filing Deadline Extended To Nov 21: Check Who Can Benefit And What It Means For Taxpayers, Businesses
 ITR Filing Deadline: The Central Board of Direct Taxes has extended the ITR filing deadline for tax audit cases from 31 October to 21 November 2026 for Assessment Year 2026-27. The extra 21 days apply only to taxpayers and eligible partners of firms whose accounts require an audit. By Sahelee Rakshit 
 Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:49 PM (IST) 
 Source: JND 
 ITR filing deadline extended to 21 November 2026 only for tax audit cases (Representational Image) Related Articles HighLights ITR filing deadline extended to 21 November 2026 only for tax audit cases.
 Non-audit taxpayers must still follow their original filing dates.
 Extra time allows completion of audits, record checks and payment of pending dues.
 ITR Filing Deadline Extended: Businesses, professionals, and other taxpayers covered under the tax audit have been given more time to file their income tax returns for Assessment Year 2026-27. The Central Board of Direct Taxes has moved the deadline from 31 October to 21 November 2026, giving them 21 extra days. The extension mainly helps those who must get their accounts audited before filing. It does not apply to everyone. People who are not covered under the tax audit rules will still have to follow their original deadlines.
 ITR Deadline Extension: Which Taxpayers Get More Time?
 The new date is only for taxpayers whose accounts need to be audited under the Income-tax Act. It also covers eligible partners of firms that require an audit. For these groups, 21 November is now the last date for filing ITRs for AY 2026-27. Others should not assume they have also received extra time and must check the deadline that applies to them.

 Complete These Financial Checks Before Filing ITR
 The extra days give businesses and professionals a chance to finish pending audit work and make sure their numbers are correct. Before filing, they should go through their books of accounts and match the figures with the financial statements and tax audit reports. Income, expenses, deductions and other details need a careful check.

 Any differences between the accounting records and the tax figures should be sorted out. Companies that follow multiple reporting requirements may need to work closely with their auditors and finance teams to clear these issues. Doing this early reduces the chance of mistakes and later corrections.
 Why Is The 21-Day Extension Important?
 For businesses that handle large transactions or keep detailed records, completing an audit and filing the return takes time. The additional three weeks help them review financial statements, double-check tax calculations and gather all required documents. It also gives auditors and finance teams more breathing space instead of rushing before the old 31 October deadline. Accurate reporting matters because wrong figures or missing details can create problems later.

 ITR Filing Before November 21: Important Things To Check
 Taxpayers who get the extension should use the time wisely. Key steps include finishing the tax audit, matching books with balance sheets and tax disclosures, verifying income and tax calculations, keeping all supporting documents ready, and clearing any pending self-assessment tax.
 They should also check whether interest under Sections 234A or 234B applies. While the new deadline offers relief, it is better not to leave everything for the last few days. Completing the audit, checking figures, and arranging paperwork early will make the filing process much smoother.
